Application.q693: HAiSP: Sprint Planning for Human-AI Agile Teams
Application.q694: This study evaluates the HAiSP (Human-Ai Sprint Planning) platform, a multi-agent system that enables human developers and AI agents to jointly conduct Agile sprint planning. We first validate the platform's automated prioritisation consensus and task assignment algorithms through fully autonomous agent-only sessions. We then recruit 15–20 experienced software practitioners to participate in mixed human-agent sprint planning sessions online, completing a post-session questionnaire grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to measure perceived usefulness, ease of use, and adoption intention. Expected outcomes include technical feasibility evidence for automated multi-agent sprint planning and empirical data on practitioner perceptions of AI agents as collaborative planning partners. Results will inform the design of AI-native Agile workflows and contribute algorithm designs to the emerging field of human-AI collaborative software engineering.

Application.q573:
As this study is conducted online via Google Meet, it may recruit software practitioners globally.

  1. Local Power and Customs: The culture relevant to this study is the global professional culture of software engineering, specifically Agile methodology, which shares standardised terminology and practices worldwide. Therefore, the risk of cultural misalignment or exploitation of local beliefs is negligible. The software effort estimation task is a widely practiced industry standard.
  2. Undue Influence and Exploitation: Participants are skilled professionals and clearly informed that there will no incentive provided for joining this study.
  3. Legal and Data Compliance: The study adheres to the strict privacy standards of the Australian National Statement and the University of Wollongong.
Application.q716: Prospective participants will receive a secure link to a Qualtrics form containing the participant information sheet, screening questions and a consent form. To submit, they must sign and upload the completed consent form. Participants will be given a week to consider their involvement voluntarily. During this consideration period, participants are free to contact the researchers via email to ask any questions they may have. The Student Investigator will be responsible for all communication and the entire consent process, from information provision to final confirmation. After one week, if no response or signed consent form is received, it will be assumed the individual is not interested in participating, and no further contact will be made regarding this research.
Application.q577:
#1 Approach to Consent and Participant Understanding

Consent will be sought via a "digital opt-in" mechanism. Participants will be provided with the Participant Information Sheet (PIS) via email. They must actively check a box or digitally sign a Consent Form prior to the commencement of the Google Meet session.

#2 Language and Literacy

The study requires participants to discuss complex technical software requirements in English. More importantly, English proficiency is a mandatory inclusion criterion. This is an operational requirement for the validity of the textual analysis, not an exclusion based on race or ethnicity.

#3 Involvement of People in Other Countries

This study offers no incentive and is clearly stated that in the PIS, hence, there is no exploitation of cheap labor or vulnerable populations often associated with international research.
Application.q585: This research have potential burdens primarily limited to time commitment and mild psychological discomfort. As the study design involves simulating effort estimation negotiation with intentional conflicting viewpoints and ambiguous tasks, participants may experience minor frustration or performance anxiety similar to that found in standard workplace meetings.
Application.q586: To mitigate this, the Participant Information Sheet will explicitly frame the session as a simulation focused on the process rather than technical capability, emphasising that there are no "correct" estimates. Participation is entirely voluntary, and participants may withdraw at any time without penalty.
Application.q587:
There will be no benefits toward the participants of this research other than having an opportunity to experience a novel approach in conducting simulated sprint planning. For the wider community, the results of this study will be beneficial in terms of:

1. Contributes to the design of future AI agents that support, rather than disrupt, human agile teams.

2. Providing insights into the how human practitioners perceive the role and benefits of affective agents in sprint planning.
Application.q588:
The potential benefits of this research are substantial for both the software engineering industry and the broader field of Human-AI Interaction. The knowledge generated will provide evidence-based guidelines for designing future AI "co-pilots" that support human well-being and reduce conflict, rather than purely logic-driven tools that may inadvertently increase workplace stress.

These significant potential benefits outweigh the minimal risks and burdens associated with the study.
Application.q589: We will transparently inform participants that the AI agents are research tools that may occasionally hallucinate or provide incorrect technical data. This manages the expectation of "AI infallibility" and prevents frustration if the agent underperforms.
